lots.what_it_is: Small boxed toy magic lantern outfit, almost certainly German-made for the English market c.1890-1910 (the printed tickets read 'Ticket for Entretainement with the Magic Lantern', the misspelt English typical of German toy-lantern exports, and the lid carries a printed instruction sheet with prize-medal motifs). Contents: nickel-plated bell-shaped lamp housing on a red-edged black plate, cast iron scroll bracket, nickel and brass lens tube, brass oil font, sheets of tickets, a bag of small parts. No glass slides: the cross straps in the lid that would hold slides are empty. Gowans title: VICTORIAN MAGIC LANTERN IN WOODEN BOX (no description). Maker not seen.

lots.key_photo_findings: Photo 1: open box with empty slide straps in lid, a bag of small parts, sheets of printed tickets 'Ticket for Entretainement with the Magic Lantern' (enlarged and read). Photo 2: nickel bell-shaped lamp housing on a red-edged black plate, cast iron scroll bracket, nickel/brass lens tube, brass oil font, printed instruction sheet with medal motifs glued in the lid (text too small to read). Photo 3: wooden box with crackled black paint finish and wear, lock escutcheon, side handle. No slides seen. No maker's name read.

lots.question_for_gowans: Are there any glass slides with it? Is there a maker's name on the lamp housing, lens or the lid instruction sheet (e.g. Ernst Plank, Bing, Schoenner)? Do the parts assemble into a complete lantern with chimney, burner and lens?
